text:
jordan_ae: FYI Rivertide POC reporting very slow first-token on hosted route (rwdx-4b). Observed ~1.4s TTFT for short prompts (~20 tokens). Target is <250ms for demo next week. Can we triage?

priya_se: Thanks — which route + config? Any recent deploys?

jordan_ae: route=rivertide-poc, default routing policy, prefill unset. No deploys in last 24h. Issue reproducible from customer region (us-west2).

lee_sre: I pulled infra traces — looks like lots of queueing at batch horizon and low prefix cache reuse. Snip from worker log around failure window: 
```
[2026-03-20T22:01:02Z] worker=wrkr-42 shard=sh-12 recv_req id=0x9a3 qdepth=18 batch_window_ms=100 batch_size=12 kv_prefill_hit=false ttft=1.39s
[2026-03-20T22:01:03Z] redis: kvcache.miss route=rivertide-poc key=prefix:abc123
[2026-03-20T22:01:03Z] worker=wrkr-42 rate_limit=429 shard_apply_delay_ms=65
```

nate_ops: Interesting, batch_window_ms=100 is large for short prompts  could cause head-of-line waiting. Also qdepth 18 suggests concurrency spike. Any per-route overrides?

priya_se: The POC used client-side retries and parallel warmup requests which may be flooding initial warmup and triggering soft rate limits. Are they doing synthetic prefill?

jordan_ae: Customer said they primed the model once but not a sustained prefill load. They do ~3 concurrent streams at demo time.

lee_sre: Hypothesis: without route-level prefill and with default large batch horizon, cold sessions group into large batches, raising avg batch latency and causing slow TTFT + occasional 429s. Also prefix caching low because sessions are unique per request (no session affinity).

compliance-bot: Questionnaire update: Rivertide asked about KMS, audit retention, SOC2, and on-prem options.

priya_se: Mitigations to try (quick): 1) set route prefill_tokens=6 2) reduce batch_window_ms to 30 3) enable session-affinity cookie for demo (so KV hits improve) 4) temporarily lower worker max_concurrency from 48 -> 24

lee_sre: I'll push a canary with batch_window_ms=30 and prefill_tokens=6 to route=rivertide-poc. Also add a short-lived quota bump to avoid 429 ripple while we warm caches.

jordan_ae: Customer also wants pricing delta for reserved capacity if we advise Dedicated-S (1 GPU) to guarantee <200ms TTFT. Need monthly and committed-annual numbers for 2x expected demo QPS.

priya_se: Ballpark: Dedicated-S covers this workload at predictable latency; rough delta ~+28% over hosted pay-as-you-go for steady 2x QPS (will get exact quote from pricing).

lee_sre: Quick before/after snapshot from canary at 22:05 (after toggles): 
```
Canary metrics 22:05: ttft_median=0.27s ttft_p95=0.42s kv_cache_hit=0.74 avg_batch_ms=34 queue_depth=6 rate_limit_events=0
Baseline 21:55: ttft_median=1.38s ttft_p95=1.7s kv_cache_hit=0.09 avg_batch_ms=98 queue_depth=17 rate_limit_events=3
```

nate_ops: Nice. Note: prefill increases token usage for each session (prefill tokens charged). We should document trade-off for the customer demo.

jordan_ae: Perfect. Can we collect perf dashboards and a short one-page explaining: what we changed, why, expected costs (prefill vs Dedicated), and recommended next steps? Need it by EOD for the bake/fix notes before the exec call.

priya_se: On it — I'll draft the one-pager with graphs and cost comparison. Also will include compliance answers: hosted KMS integrations supported (AWS/GCP), audit logs default 90d retention, Private supports HSM/on-prem.

lee_sre: Action list: me = push canary & monitor 2h; nate = request temporary shard quota bump + monitor rate limits; priya = pricing + one-pager; jordan = schedule demo follow-up.

jordan_ae: Thanks team — really appreciate the quick turnaround. :party_parrot:

lee_sre: I'll post 2h dashboard snapshot here when complete.

nate_ops: quota bump request submitted to infra-ops ticket #INF-4672. ETA ~45m.

jordan_ae: Great, keep me posted.

priya_se: Draft ready, uploading graphs now. Will attach in thread in ~10m. :white_check_mark:
